note: Snapshot of the hosted server's tools/list, served only when no AGENTXRAY_TOKEN is set. Refresh: npm run catalog.

tools.name: daily_brief
tools.title: Today's brief (spoken)
tools.description: How today is going for the connected Amazon seller account, as ONE short paragraph written to be read aloud: units sold so far today in the store's own time zone, the money Amazon has actually POSTED recently (today's fees do not exist yet — they post 7.5-13 days after purchase), ad spend, and at most two things that need attention. Use this for 'how did today go', 'what happened today', 'give me my morning brief'. The result carries a 'narrative' field that is already composed from measured numbers: read it out word for word and do not recompute, re-round or add numbers of your own.

marketplace_id.description: Optional. Only needed when more than one marketplace is connected; the brief names the choices itself.

tools.name: list_my_accounts
tools.title: List connected seller accounts
tools.description: List the Amazon seller accounts connected to this workspace, with the marketplaces each one covers. An agency has one per client; a single seller has one. Every marketplace-scoped tool takes an 'account' argument naming which of them to answer about, and refuses rather than guessing when several could apply.

tools.name: list_my_marketplaces
tools.title: List connected marketplaces
tools.description: List the Amazon marketplaces on the seller account connected to this AgentXray workspace. Call this FIRST whenever a question needs a marketplace id (Buy Box, inventory age) so you never guess one.

tools.name: get_profit_summary
tools.title: Profit summary (measured)
tools.description: Real profit and loss for the connected Amazon seller account over a window: revenue, Amazon fees, COGS, net profit and margin, grouped per currency. Numbers come from posted Amazon fee events joined to the seller's own orders and saved product costs, so fees include the consumption tax Amazon actually charged (such as AU GST). Use this for 'what did I actually make', 'was last month profitable', 'what are my fees'.

date.description: ONE calendar day instead of a window: 'yesterday', 'today' or YYYY-MM-DD (within the last 365 days). The day is the STORE's own day in its marketplace's timezone. Use it for 'how was yesterday' or a named date; do not also pass days.

start_date.description: First day of a custom range, YYYY-MM-DD on the STORE's calendar (inclusive). Pass with end_date for 'September', 'between X and Y' or any past period; it replaces days. At most 730 days.

end_date.description: Last day of the custom range, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive).

marketplace_id.description: Optional marketplace filter (e.g. ATVPDKIKX0DER).

tools.name: get_reorder_plan
tools.title: What to reorder, and from whom
tools.description: What to reorder, how much, by when and from whom, per SKU: stock (Amazon's, or the seller's own shelf for merchant-fulfilled listings), the 30-day sales rate, days until it runs out, the lead time used and where it came from, the supplier and their minimum order. Use it for 'what should I reorder' and 'when do I run out'.

marketplace_id.description: Marketplace (inferred when only one is connected).

limit.description: Max SKUs (default 20, max 50), soonest to run out first.

annotations.title: What to reorder, and from whom

tools.name: get_profit_by_sku
tools.title: Profit by SKU
tools.description: Per-SKU profit ranking for the connected seller account over a window: units, revenue, fees, COGS, net profit and margin per SKU. Use this for 'which product makes money', 'which SKU is losing money', 'what should I stop selling'.

days.description: Window in days, 1-365 (default 7, as the app).

date.description: ONE calendar day instead of a window: 'yesterday', 'today' or YYYY-MM-DD (within the last 365 days). The day is the STORE's own day in its marketplace's timezone. Use it for 'how was yesterday' or a named date; do not also pass days.

start_date.description: First day of a custom range, YYYY-MM-DD on the STORE's calendar (inclusive). Pass with end_date for 'September', 'between X and Y' or any past period; it replaces days. At most 730 days.

end_date.description: Last day of the custom range, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive).

marketplace_id.description: Optional marketplace filter.

tools.name: get_traffic_and_conversion
tools.title: Sessions and conversion per ASIN
tools.description: Sessions, page views and conversion rate per ASIN from Amazon's Sales & Traffic report, for the connected seller account. This is the metric that separates the two halves of the funnel: clicks with no orders can be a targeting problem OR a detail-page problem, and unit-session percentage is the only field that tells them apart. Conversion is computed from the window's summed units and sessions. Check it before recommending any listing change.

start_date.description: First day of a custom range, YYYY-MM-DD on the STORE's calendar (inclusive). Pass with end_date for 'September', 'between X and Y' or any past period; it replaces days. At most 730 days.

end_date.description: Last day of the custom range, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive).

marketplace_id.description: Optional marketplace filter.

tools.name: get_buybox_status
tools.title: Buy Box status
tools.description: Buy Box performance for one marketplace on the connected seller account: win rate over a window, SKUs currently losing the Buy Box with the competing price gap, recent held-to-lost transitions, and per listing how many sellers offer it, who holds the Buy Box and each other seller's price, FBA/Prime and feedback with a storefront link (listing_competition; read its summary out first). A listing Amazon returned no offer data for is unmeasured, never 'only seller'. Requires a marketplace id from list_my_marketplaces.

marketplace_id.description: Required marketplace id (from list_my_marketplaces).

account.description: Seller id of the client account to act on (from list_my_accounts). Only needed when more than one connected account covers this marketplace — an agency. Omit it and a single account resolves by itself; omit it with several and the tool refuses rather than guessing which client you meant.

tools.name: get_stock_history
tools.title: Stock history and stock-outs
tools.description: How long one SKU has been in stock on one marketplace and what running out cost: days in stock, out of stock, not launched yet and unknown (no snapshot), each stock-out period, the first receipt, units per day on in-stock days only, and an ESTIMATE of sales lost while out of stock. Use it for 'how long has this been selling', 'how many days was it out of stock', 'what did running out cost'.

sku.description: The seller SKU.

marketplace_id.description: Marketplace (inferred when only one is connected).

account.description: Seller id of the client account (agencies with several accounts on this marketplace).

tools.name: get_sku_trend
tools.title: One product over time
tools.description: One SKU over time on one marketplace: units per day, the price buyers actually paid after promotions against the listed price, sessions, conversion and Buy Box %, and settled net profit per week. Use it for 'how is this product doing over time', 'did my price change hurt conversion', 'what do buyers really pay'.

sku.description: The seller SKU.

marketplace_id.description: Marketplace (inferred when only one is connected).

account.description: Seller id of the client account (agencies with several accounts on this marketplace).

tools.name: get_bsr_history
tools.title: Best Seller Rank over time
tools.description: Best Seller Rank over time for your own products: one point per day, the category, the 7- and 30-day change, and whether the latest day is a sharp drop, a rise or steady (lower rank is better). History starts the day AgentXray first read the product. Use it for 'is my rank going up or down', 'which products lost rank this week'.

sku.description: One seller SKU for its daily series (omit to list every tracked product).

marketplace_id.description: Marketplace (inferred when only one is connected).

account.description: Seller id of the client account (agencies with several accounts on this marketplace).

tools.name: get_inventory_age
tools.title: FBA inventory age
tools.description: FBA inventory age for one marketplace on the connected seller account: how stock is distributed across age buckets and which SKUs are approaching long-term storage fees. Use this for 'is my stock getting old', 'will I be charged storage fees'. Requires a marketplace id from list_my_marketplaces.

marketplace_id.description: Required marketplace id (from list_my_marketplaces).

account.description: Seller id of the client account to act on (from list_my_accounts). Only needed when more than one connected account covers this marketplace — an agency. Omit it and a single account resolves by itself; omit it with several and the tool refuses rather than guessing which client you meant.

tools.name: get_payout_balance
tools.title: Payout balance and why it moved
tools.description: The seller's Amazon payout balance and why it moved, from Amazon's own settlement lines: what the current settlement started from (negative = still owed to Amazon), what is released and held now, and the last settlements broken into buckets with the posting date of every advertising invoice, debt adjustment and carried balance. Use it for 'why is my balance negative', 'what triggered −X', 'what did Amazon deduct', 'when do I get paid'. Money only — units live in get_inventory_reconciliation.

marketplace_id.description: Marketplace id (from list_my_marketplaces); inferred when the seller has one.

payouts.description: How many recent settlements to break down (default 4, max 12).

account.description: Seller id of the client account (from list_my_accounts). Only needed when several connected accounts cover this marketplace; with several and no account the tool refuses rather than guessing.

annotations.title: Payout balance and why it moved

tools.name: get_inventory_reconciliation
tools.title: Unreconciled inventory (Amazon's own column)
tools.description: UNITS ONLY — says nothing about money, balances or payouts (use get_payout_balance for money). Units Amazon's own Inventory Ledger has not reconciled for one marketplace on the connected seller account, with Amazon's reference id for each row, plus the ledger's event totals in units (receipts, shipments, adjustments). Use this for 'am I missing units', 'is Amazon holding stock it never accounted for'. This reads Amazon's own Unreconciled Quantity column — it does not derive a shortfall from a formula. Requires a marketplace id from list_my_marketplaces.

marketplace_id.description: Required marketplace id (from list_my_marketplaces).

sku.description: Optional: limit to one seller SKU.

account.description: Seller id of the client account to act on (from list_my_accounts). Only needed when more than one connected account covers this marketplace.

tools.name: get_my_brands
tools.title: Registered brands
tools.description: Brands registered to this seller in Amazon Brand Registry, with the brand entity id, as Amazon's Advertising API reports them. Call this before proposing anything brand-gated — Sponsored Brands, A+ Content, Brand Analytics and Vine all require an enrolled brand. An empty list distinguishes 'no brand enrolled' from 'not synced yet'.

account.description: Seller id of the client account (from list_my_accounts). Only needed with several accounts.

tools.name: get_brand_search_terms
tools.title: Amazon weekly search-term ranking
tools.description: Amazon's own weekly Brand Analytics search-term ranking for one marketplace on the connected seller account: which customer search terms rank where, the ASINs shoppers clicked on each, and how each term moved against the previous week. Rank 1 is the most-searched term, so a smaller rank is better. Requires Brand Registry; an unenrolled seller gets a named refusal rather than an estimate. Requires a marketplace id from list_my_marketplaces.

marketplace_id.description: Required marketplace id (from list_my_marketplaces).

search_term.description: Optional: only terms containing this text.

account.description: Seller id of the client account (from list_my_accounts). Only needed with several accounts.

tools.name: get_ads_campaigns
tools.title: Ad campaigns with ids and budgets
tools.description: Campaigns on the connected Amazon Ads account WITH their Amazon campaign ids, state, daily budget, measured spend and sales, and budget utilisation. Call this before proposing a budget or a pause: both need the campaign id, and utilisation is what a budget decision turns on — a campaign running at 40% of its budget is not budget-constrained, so raising it buys nothing.

marketplace_id.description: Optional. Scope to ONE marketplace. Omit only when the seller has a single marketplace, or when they really do mean every market at once — figures from different marketplaces are in different currencies and are never converted. Call list_my_marketplaces first.

state.description: Which campaigns to list (default enabled: paused and archived campaigns spend nothing). counts_by_state always counts every state regardless.

annotations.title: Ad campaigns with ids and budgets

tools.name: get_ads_targets
tools.title: Ad targets with ids and bids
tools.description: Keyword and product targets WITH their Amazon target ids, current bid, ad group and campaign ids, and measured clicks, orders, spend and sales. Call this before proposing a bid change: the clicks and orders are what let the proposal be priced against this seller's own break-even CPC rather than a rule of thumb.

marketplace_id.description: Optional. Scope to ONE marketplace. Omit only when the seller has a single marketplace, or when they really do mean every market at once — figures from different marketplaces are in different currencies and are never converted. Call list_my_marketplaces first.

annotations.title: Ad targets with ids and bids

tools.name: get_ads_search_terms
tools.title: Search terms with spend
tools.description: Customer search terms that triggered ads, with clicks, orders and spend, the campaign and ad group they came through, and whether each is ALREADY negated. Call this before proposing a negative keyword. Zero orders on single-digit clicks is not evidence of a bad term — it is what a normal conversion rate looks like most of the time.

marketplace_id.description: Optional. Scope to ONE marketplace. Omit only when the seller has a single marketplace, or when they really do mean every market at once — figures from different marketplaces are in different currencies and are never converted. Call list_my_marketplaces first.

tools.name: get_ads_overview
tools.title: Amazon Ads overview
tools.description: Amazon Advertising performance for the connected account: whether the Ads connection exists, and per-campaign spend, sales, clicks, orders, ACoS and ROAS over a window. Ad spend is billed separately from Amazon settlements, so it is NOT part of the profit tools — call this as well when a question is about total profitability.

marketplace_id.description: Optional. Scope to ONE marketplace. Omit only when the seller has a single marketplace, or when they really do mean every market at once — figures from different marketplaces are in different currencies and are never converted. Call list_my_marketplaces first.

tools.name: get_ad_group_profit
tools.title: Net contribution per ad group
tools.description: Net contribution per ad group, priced with the seller's own economics measured from their settlement (price, Amazon fees, storage, saved unit costs): spend, ad sales, ACoS, CPC, the highest CPC each ad group can afford, and kill candidates. Read its `narrative` as the answer.

marketplace_id.description: Marketplace (inferred when only one is connected).

sku.description: Optional: only the ad groups that advertised this SKU, priced at its own margin.

tools.name: get_ads_by_product
tools.title: Ad spend and net contribution per product
tools.description: Advertising per product (advertised SKU): each SKU's own spend, ad sales, ACoS, its measured break-even and the net contribution its ads made after Amazon fees, product cost and ads. Read its `narrative` as the answer.

marketplace_id.description: Marketplace (inferred when only one is connected).

annotations.title: Ad spend and net contribution per product

tools.name: get_ads_search_term_verdicts
tools.title: Wasted, winning and harvestable search terms
tools.description: Search terms judged over every term: wasted (twice the account's clicks-per-order and no order), best sellers against the measured break-even, and harvest candidates not yet an exact keyword. Read its `narrative` as the answer.

marketplace_id.description: Marketplace (inferred when only one is connected).

annotations.title: Wasted, winning and harvestable search terms

tools.name: get_ads_placements
tools.title: Top-of-Search share per campaign
tools.description: Top-of-Search impression share and placement stats per campaign, from Amazon's own spCampaigns daily reports: share of eligible top-of-search impressions won, plus top-of-search impressions, clicks and spend against total impressions. Use for visibility questions — why impressions are flat, whether a campaign shows at the top of search. Absence from the result means no report rows in the window, not zero share.

tools.name: get_ads_daily_series
tools.title: Daily ad spend and ACoS
tools.description: Per-DAY advertising spend, sales, clicks and ACoS — the series that answers 'when did it change', which a 30-day rollup cannot. Use for pacing, for finding the day a change took effect, and before claiming any trend. A day Amazon did not report is ABSENT, not zero.

marketplace_id.description: Optional. Scope to ONE marketplace. Omit only when the seller has a single marketplace, or when they really do mean every market at once — figures from different marketplaces are in different currencies and are never converted. Call list_my_marketplaces first.

campaign_id.description: Amazon campaign id, to get one campaign's own series.

tools.name: get_ads_negatives
tools.title: Negative keywords on the account
tools.description: Every negative keyword on the account, with its campaign and ad group and a self_block flag. self_block means the seller also bids on that exact term in the same ad group — the campaign blocks a keyword it pays for. A negative is invisible by construction, so this list is the only way to see one.

marketplace_id.description: Optional. Scope to ONE marketplace. Omit only when the seller has a single marketplace, or when they really do mean every market at once — figures from different marketplaces are in different currencies and are never converted. Call list_my_marketplaces first.

tools.name: get_my_changes
tools.title: Your applied changes and their verdicts
tools.description: Changes applied through AgentXray and where each stands in its proof: the 14-day net-contribution verdict, or status 'measuring' when the window has not matured; `amazon_state` says where Amazon stands on each (sent / amazon_processing / verified / problem) — Amazon accepting a change is not the change being live; plus `waiting_for_approval`, the drafts not yet approved, and `journal`: every draft, rejection (with the seller's reason) and Amazon outcome in order, with `open_measurements` — read it before drafting more, never re-propose what was rejected. Use before claiming a past change worked.

sku.description: Only this SKU's history (journal and changes).

since_days.description: How far back the journal reads (default 60, max 365).

annotations.title: Your applied changes and their verdicts

tools.name: get_amazon_bid_recommendations
tools.title: Amazon suggested bid range
tools.description: AMAZON's own suggested bid range for the live keywords in one ad group - what the auction currently costs. A DIFFERENT number from the seller's break-even CPC, which is priced against their measured margin. Report both, say which is which, never average them.

ad_group_id.description: Amazon ad group id (from get_ads_targets). This alone identifies the account and marketplace — do not pass one separately.

tools.name: get_my_product_costs
tools.title: Saved product costs (COGS)
tools.description: The product costs (COGS) saved in this AgentXray workspace: SKU, marketplace, unit cost, currency and validity dates. Call this when a profit answer depends on whether costs are actually recorded — a SKU with no saved cost is counted at zero cost, which makes profit look better than it is.

tools.name: did_my_changes_work
tools.title: Did my changes work?
tools.description: The MEASURED outcome of changes this seller approved and applied through AgentXray: what changed, when, and what happened to conversion in the fortnight afterwards. Verdicts are deliberately conservative — at low volume 'inconclusive' is the honest answer and the reasons say exactly why (thin traffic, day-to-day swing, another change to the same listing inside the window). A change whose window has not closed yet reports status 'measuring' with the date it can first be read. Use for 'did that change work', 'was it worth it'.

tools.name: what_i_cannot_tell_you
tools.title: What I cannot tell you
tools.description: The honest limits of this account's data, measured live for the connected seller: which SKUs have unrecorded costs (profit overstated), how many recent orders Amazon has not fully posted yet, whether ad spend is invisible, and the structural limits that apply to everyone. Call this BEFORE drawing conclusions from the other tools, and whenever the seller asks how much to trust the numbers.

tools.name: get_account_health
tools.title: Account health and open problems
tools.description: Account health for each connected Amazon seller account: Amazon's own Account Health rating and account status, every problem the latest check found (with the SKUs it touches and what to do), and unacknowledged alerts of the last 14 days. Use it for 'is my account healthy', 'am I at risk of suspension', 'any policy problems'. Its `narrative` is the answer.

tools.name: get_inbound_shipments
tools.title: FBA shipments on the way or received short
tools.description: FBA inbound shipments: which are on their way, units sent vs units Amazon has received, status and destination warehouse, and closed shipments where Amazon received fewer units than were sent. Use it for 'where is my shipment', 'has Amazon received my stock', 'is anything missing from a shipment'. Its `narrative` is the answer.

marketplace_id.description: Optional: one marketplace only.

annotations.title: FBA shipments on the way or received short

tools.name: get_listing_issues
tools.title: Listings with Amazon errors or not buyable
tools.description: Listings with problems Amazon reported (errors that block a listing from selling, and warnings), with Amazon's own message per SKU, and listing deadlines that are still open. A listing that is simply not buyable (often no stock) is counted separately, not reported as a problem. Use it for 'are any of my listings suppressed', 'listing errors', 'why can't my product be bought'. Its `narrative` is the answer.

marketplace_id.description: Optional: one marketplace only.

annotations.title: Listings with Amazon errors or not buyable

tools.name: get_listing_fix_plan
tools.title: One listing's problems and the exact fix for each
tools.description: One listing's problems with the exact fix for each, read LIVE from Amazon: which door fixes it (draft the text, draft an attribute, a new image, a Seller Central case with the case text ready, or a category approval), how bad it is (not sellable / hidden from search / attribute hidden), and for every attribute an issue names, what Amazon's product-type schema requires (sub-fields, allowed values, limits), the current value and a value skeleton in the exact patch shape. Use it after get_listing_issues, before drafting any listing fix. Its `narrative` is the answer.

sku.description: The seller SKU.

marketplace_id.description: The marketplace of that listing.

account.description: Seller id of the client account (agencies).

annotations.title: One listing's problems and the exact fix for each

tools.name: get_listing_images
tools.title: One listing's image slots, shown, against the six image roles
tools.description: One listing's image slots read LIVE from Amazon (main + 8), with the pictures themselves so you can see them: what buyers are shown per slot, size and zoom, empty slots, images Amazon has flagged, and slots where another contributor's image wins over the seller's. Returns the six roles a complete image stack fills (main image that wins the click, what's in the box, the difference, a five-second infographic, lifestyle in use, the objection handler). Look at the images, say which role each fills and which roles are missing; draft a replacement with draft_image_swap once the seller has the new image. Its `narrative` is the measured part.

sku.description: The seller SKU.

marketplace_id.description: The marketplace of that listing.

account.description: Seller id of the client account (agencies).

annotations.title: One listing's image slots, shown, against the six image roles

tools.name: get_returns
tools.title: Returns, return rate and reasons
tools.description: Customer returns for one marketplace over a window: units returned against units sold in the same window (a same-window rate), the most returned products, the reasons Amazon recorded and customers' own comments. Use it for 'how many returns', 'why are customers returning', 'which product has the most returns'. Its `narrative` is the answer.

marketplace_id.description: Marketplace (inferred when only one is connected).

tools.name: get_orders
tools.title: Orders, units and cancellations by day
tools.description: Orders for one marketplace over the last N days (default 7, max 30), by the store's own calendar day. days=1 is TODAY so far only; for yesterday or any single date pass day='yesterday' / day='YYYY-MM-DD'. Never call a day with no orders in the result a zero day unless it is inside first_day..last_day. Returns orders, units, cancelled, still unshipped, order value by currency, the best-selling SKUs and the most recent orders with their status. Never includes the buyer's name or address — AgentXray does not hold them. Pending orders have no final value yet and are counted, not priced. For profit use get_profit_summary.

marketplace_id.description: Required when the account has more than one store with sales.

days.description: Window in days, 1–30 (default 7). 1 = today so far.

day.description: One store day instead of a window: 'today', 'yesterday' or YYYY-MM-DD.

annotations.title: Orders, units and cancellations by day

tools.name: get_review_requests
tools.title: Review requests sent and orders still askable
tools.description: Amazon 'Request a Review' solicitations on the connected account: how many were sent (last 30 days and in total), orders that can still be asked, why requests did not go out, and whether AgentXray sends them automatically. The last send date and the purchase dates of askable orders are included. Use it for 'did my buyers get review requests', 'how many review requests did I send', 'can I ask for more reviews'. To send, draft_review_requests. Its `narrative` is the answer.

marketplace_id.description: Optional: one marketplace only.

annotations.title: Review requests sent and orders still askable

tools.name: get_ads_recommendations
tools.title: Ads recommendations (with ready drafts)
tools.description: What to change in Sponsored Products now, and why: bid cuts and raises against each target's own measured break-even CPC, search terms to negate (clicks with no order), converting search terms to add as EXACT keywords, budget raises and cuts, placement adjustments, and campaigns to pause because every advertised product is out of stock. Each item carries its evidence, the risk screen a draft would get, and a ready `draft` ({tool, args}) — file it with that draft tool ONLY after the seller agrees, then offer schedule_follow_up on `follow_up_on` (the 14-day verdict day). Reading this changes nothing. Use it for 'what should I change in my ads', 'optimise my PPC', 'audit my campaigns'.

marketplace_id.description: Marketplace (inferred when only one is connected).

account.description: Seller id of the client account (agencies with several accounts on this marketplace).

tools.name: get_tacos
tools.title: TACoS: ads vs all sales
tools.description: TACoS — ad spend divided by ALL sales ordered in the same store days — in total and per SKU, beside ACoS (ad spend ÷ ad-attributed sales) and the share of each SKU's sales the ads claim. Use it for 'what is my TACoS', 'how dependent am I on ads', 'are my organic sales growing'. Organic sales are DERIVED (ordered sales − ad-attributed sales) and labelled so.

marketplace_id.description: Marketplace (inferred when only one is connected).

account.description: Seller id of the client account (agencies with several accounts on this marketplace).

tools.name: get_change_scorecard
tools.title: What has worked (change scorecard)
tools.description: What kind of change has worked on THIS account: every change applied through AgentXray, grouped by type (bid, negative, budget, placement, listing, price…) and by who drafted it, with how many moved net contribution up, down, were inconclusive, had no data, or are still measuring, and the summed net contribution of the judged ones. Use it before recommending a kind of change, and for 'what has worked', 'is the AI helping'.

tools.name: get_product_target_performance
tools.title: Product targets vs competitors
tools.description: Product (ASIN) and category targets: clicks, orders, spend and sales per target, its measured break-even CPC against its bid, and — when that ASIN is a watched competitor — its latest Buy Box price, offer count and weakness signal. Use it for 'which competitor ASINs should I target', 'are my product targets profitable', 'is the competitor I target out of stock'.

marketplace_id.description: Marketplace (inferred when only one is connected).

account.description: Seller id of the client account (agencies with several accounts on this marketplace).

tools.name: get_sponsored_brands
tools.title: Sponsored Brands (measured)
tools.description: Sponsored Brands campaigns (brand-registered sellers): spend, sales, ACoS, orders, and new-to-brand orders and sales per campaign over a window, from Amazon's own Sponsored Brands report. Says whether SB was collected at all for this store — no campaign and never collected are different answers. Use it for 'how are my Sponsored Brands ads doing', 'how many new customers do my brand ads bring'.

marketplace_id.description: Marketplace (inferred when only one is connected).

account.description: Seller id of the client account (agencies with several accounts on this marketplace).

tools.name: get_sponsored_display
tools.title: Sponsored Display (measured)
tools.description: Sponsored Display campaigns: spend, sales, ACoS, orders, detail page views and new-to-brand orders per campaign over a window, from Amazon's own Sponsored Display report. Display sales include view-through purchases under Amazon's attribution, so they are not comparable one-to-one with Sponsored Products. Use it for 'how are my display ads doing', 'is retargeting worth it'.

marketplace_id.description: Marketplace (inferred when only one is connected).

account.description: Seller id of the client account (agencies with several accounts on this marketplace).

tools.name: get_brand_keyword_gaps
tools.title: Brand keyword gaps (with ready drafts)
tools.description: Brand Analytics, analysed (brand-registered sellers): (1) search terms where this seller's product gets a click share like a competitor's but a lower conversion share — a detail-page problem (price, reviews, images), not a keyword one; (2) search terms the seller's own buyers use that the listing's title, bullets and backend keywords do not carry, each with a ready `draft` (draft_listing_update carrying the FULL backend keyword set — the field is replaced, never appended). File a draft only after the seller agrees. Use it for 'which keywords am I missing', 'why do competitors convert better', 'improve my listing for search'.

marketplace_id.description: Marketplace (inferred when only one is connected).

account.description: Seller id of the client account (agencies with several accounts on this marketplace).

tools.name: get_search_term_history
tools.title: Search term history (Brand Analytics)
tools.description: Search frequency rank of Brand Analytics search terms week by week (1 = most searched), with this seller's own click share and conversion share on the term in each week they appear in its top three. tools.name: draft_listing_update
tools.title: Draft a listing update (needs seller approval)
tools.description: Draft a change to a listing's title (item_name), bullet points, product description and/or backend search terms (generic_keyword) on the connected Amazon account. To change a listing's IMAGES use draft_image_swap instead. This NEVER edits the live listing: it creates a draft that the seller must review and approve in AgentXray (your Inbox (Approvals tab)) before anything is sent to Amazon. The draft is screened against Amazon policy and trademark rules; blocking risks come back in the response — revise and submit a new draft if so. Hard limits: item_name max 75 characters INCLUDING spaces; up to 5 bullet points; product_description max 2000 characters; generic_keyword max 250 BYTES (not characters) and it REPLACES the existing search terms, so send the full set you want, never just the additions. Any OTHER product attribute (unit_count, fabric_type, manufacturer...) goes in `attributes`, in the exact shape get_listing_fix_plan returns as value_skeleton; it is checked against Amazon's product-type schema before the draft exists. Every draft is then run through Amazon's own validation preview, and a draft Amazon would reject cannot be approved.

sku.description: The seller SKU to edit.

sources.description: PRODUCT-FACTS-1: for each field you set, where the value came from, quoted: e.g. {"item_name": "Amazon's name: PLANET BABY Cloth Diapers …", "unit_count": "Amazon's name says 'Quantity 6'"}. Take them from get_listing_fix_plan suggestions or from what the seller told you. The seller sees them before approving; a field without a source is flagged.

attributes.description: Other product attributes, {attribute_name: [entries]}, each entry in Amazon's patch shape, e.g. {"unit_count": [{"value": 50, "type": {"value": "count", "language_tag": "en_CA"}, "marketplace_id": "A2EUQ1WTGCTBG2"}]}. Take the shape from get_listing_fix_plan; never invent a value the seller has not confirmed (a real count, a real material).

product_description.description: Proposed product description, max 2000 chars. Plain text — Amazon strips most HTML here.

generic_keyword.description: Proposed backend search terms, space separated, max 250 BYTES. Never shown to customers. REPLACES the current terms — send the complete set, not just new words.

This NEVER changes the live price: it creates a draft the seller must review and approve in AgentXray (the Approvals page in the sidebar). The draft reads the current price from Amazon and reports what the new price does to the seller's measured break-even ACoS — read that back verbatim, because every bid and budget decision on the account was derived from the OLD price. It changes the regular price only: if a sale or coupon is running, buyers keep paying the sale price until that window ends, and the draft says so. Not for Business/B2B pricing.

tools.name: draft_image_swap
tools.title: Draft an image swap (needs seller approval)
tools.description: Draft a replacement for one or more of a listing's images on the connected Amazon account. This NEVER edits the live listing: it creates a draft the seller must review and approve in AgentXray (your Inbox (Approvals tab)) before anything is sent to Amazon. Give a public https URL per slot — 'main' for the hero image, '1' to '8' for the secondary ones. Each URL is FETCHED AND MEASURED before the draft is approvable (format, dimensions, and for the main slot the background), and whatever fails comes back in the risk list with the measured value. Amazon needs at least 500px on the longest side and 1600px for detail-page zoom. Note that a main image Amazon's classifier rejects can SUPPRESS the listing, which is worse than a failed validation — say so when you propose one.

Required: marketplace_id, a NEW sku, product_type (Amazon's UPPER_SNAKE type, e.g. ENVELOPE), item_name (≤75 chars incl. spaces), price (marketplace currency), and images.main (public https URL — fetched and measured before drafting). Optional: brand (default Generic; branded creates usually need Brand Registry), bullet_points (≤5), product_description (≤2000), images '1'..'8'. Product-type schemas vary; when the preview lists missing attributes, re-draft with them in extra_attributes. Tell the seller to run the PREVIEW in the panel: Amazon lists every missing attribute for that type without creating anything. If the sku already exists the draft is blocked; use draft_listing_update instead.

tools.name: draft_shipment_plan
tools.title: Draft an FBA shipment plan (needs seller approval)
tools.description: Draft an inbound FBA shipment for the seller to approve. This NEVER creates anything on Amazon by itself: it checks the plan against the constraints that actually get shipments rejected and puts it in front of the seller in AgentXray (your Inbox (Approvals tab)). Storage-capacity checking (Amazon measures it in CUBIC METRES, not units) is only active on marketplaces where the account's confirmed limit is on file — today that is Australia. Elsewhere the draft says the limit is unknown rather than implying the plan fits. On approval it creates a DRAFT inbound plan in their Amazon account; they then finish packing, placement and carrier steps in Seller Central, where Amazon shows the real costs. Nothing is defaulted: a ship-from address and carton dimensions must come from the seller or from a saved supplier quote. Do not invent them — a guessed address does not fail loudly.

prep_owner.description: SELLER or AMAZON — who pays for prep.

Never guess any of it. `name` is the supplier company; `contact_name` is the PERSON there (usually the sales rep answering the seller's messages) — Amazon and the carrier need someone to call, and the two are different fields.

tools.name: draft_add_product_targets
tools.title: Draft targeting competitor ASINs (needs seller approval)
tools.description: Draft adding product (ASIN) targets to an EXISTING ad group - this is how a seller advertises on a competitor's product page. Send the ASINs as one array in one draft. All targets in a draft share one bid. A product target only serves where Amazon judges the seller's product relevant to the targeted page, so zero impressions can mean irrelevance rather than a low bid; say that rather than recommending a bid raise straight away.

account.description: Seller id of the client account (agencies with several accounts on this marketplace — call list_my_accounts). Omit when there is only one.

tools.name: draft_create_product_ad
tools.title: Draft advertising a SKU in an ad group (needs seller approval)
tools.description: Draft putting a SKU into an ad group as a product ad. This is the step that makes a campaign actually advertise something: a campaign with keywords or targets but NO product ad never serves and never spends, and looks launched until somebody checks. If the seller has just created a campaign, this is the next call.

sku.description: The seller SKU to advertise.

account.description: Seller id of the client account (agencies with several accounts on this marketplace — call list_my_accounts). Omit when there is only one.

tools.name: draft_review_requests
tools.title: Draft Amazon review requests to recent buyers (needs seller approval)
tools.description: Draft Amazon's own 'Request a Review' for the seller's recent FBA orders that have not been asked yet (purchased about 3-30 days ago, shipped). This NEVER contacts a buyer by itself: it lists the eligible orders and puts ONE draft in the seller's AgentXray Inbox (Approvals tab). Only after a person approves it does AgentXray ask Amazon, order by order, whether a request is allowed right now and send it — Amazon emails each buyer once, in Amazon's own wording, and a sent request cannot be withdrawn. The approval result counts sent / not eligible yet / already requested. At most 30 orders per draft (sending takes about 1-2 seconds per order); when more are eligible the result says so — draft again after this one is approved. Call get_review_requests first to see what was already sent.

marketplace_id.description: Optional: one marketplace only (from list_my_marketplaces).

max_orders.description: Orders in this draft, 1-30 (default 25), oldest first.

account.description: Seller id of the client account (agencies with several accounts on this marketplace — call list_my_accounts). Omit when there is only one.

tools.name: draft_listing_fixes
tools.title: Draft listing fixes for many SKUs (needs seller approval)
tools.description: Draft the same kind of listing fix for up to 25 SKUs at once — e.g. the 45 listings get_listing_issues reports as not sellable for a missing title, or 29 missing a unit count. Each item takes the same fields as draft_listing_update (item_name, bullet_points, product_description, generic_keyword, attributes) and becomes its OWN draft: each is checked against Amazon's schema and Amazon's validation preview separately, so one bad item never blocks the rest. The seller approves them in AgentXray (Inbox → Approvals, 'Approve all'). Nothing reaches Amazon before that.

items.description: One object per SKU, each with marketplace_id, sku and the fields to change.

account.description: Seller id of the client account (agencies with several accounts on this marketplace — call list_my_accounts). Omit when there is only one.

annotations.title: Draft listing fixes for many SKUs (needs seller approval)
